note: How an engagement is actually shaped. The opportunity itself is generated from what Lyzr has delivered; these are the commitments underneath it, and a model never writes them. {unit} is the one thing the pilot runs on, supplied per line and capped at four words: one approval chain, one hiring flow, one business unit. `revenue` is the three streams the brief tables, written here for the same reason.

patterns.when: The client already runs the process and the partner already works inside it. The question is which part of it stops being manual first.

first_offer.name: {work} assessment
first_offer.ends_with: the process mapped end to end with the manual steps costed, and a scoped pilot on one of them

delivery.shape: 8 to 10 week build on one {unit}, then a managed fee to run and extend it

patterns.expansion: A monthly fee to run it, then the same pattern on the next {unit} in the same account
discovery: How many {unit}s go through this today, and how often
Which steps are already rule-based, and which need judgement
Which systems hold the data the steps read
Who approves an exception today, and how it reaches them

roles.partner: The process knowledge, the client relationship, the integration and the delivery team
roles.lyzr: The platform the agents run on, the controls, and support through the first build

revenue.implementation: Process mapping, solution design, agent configuration, integration with the systems the {unit} already runs on, and deployment of the first build
revenue.recurring: Running the agents, handling the exceptions, tuning as the process changes, and support for the people who use it
revenue.expansion: The same pattern on the next {unit} in the same account, then the adjacent processes as they come up

patterns.when: The work is technically uncertain rather than commercially uncertain. Prove it on one narrow case, then sell the rollout.

first_offer.name: {work} feasibility proof
first_offer.ends_with: a working proof on one {unit}, with the accuracy measured against their own examples

delivery.shape: 6 week proof on one {unit}, then a per-{unit} rollout
delivery.team_needed: 1 engineer + 1 person from the client who knows the exceptions

patterns.expansion: Each further {unit} is a shorter build on the same proven pattern
discovery: How many {unit}s exist, and which are highest volume
What a correct result looks like, and who decides that today
Which systems the result has to be written back into
What accuracy would have to be true before they trust it unattended

roles.partner: The client's examples, the integration work and the people who judge the output
roles.lyzr: The platform, the models and the engineer who sits with you through the proof

revenue.implementation: The feasibility proof on one {unit}, then the build that follows it: solution design, integration, testing and release
revenue.recurring: Monitoring each live {unit}, tuning the models, and support through every rollout wave
revenue.expansion: Each further {unit} as a shorter build on the proven pattern, with no new architecture to pay for

patterns.when: A packaged offer for a client the partner does not have yet. The audit is the way in, and it has to be worth paying for on its own.

first_offer.name: {work} audit
first_offer.ends_with: where the time actually goes in one {unit}, and a scoped build on the worst of it

delivery.shape: 6 week build on one {unit}, then recurring per {unit}
delivery.team_needed: 1 consultant who knows the domain + 1 engineer

patterns.expansion: The second {unit} is a shorter build, and the audit becomes the repeatable way in to the next client
discovery: How much of this work happens in a month, and who does it
Which parts are judgement and which are the same every time
What the output has to look like, and who signs it
What they have already tried here, and why it stopped

roles.partner: The domain expertise, the audit, the build and the client relationship
roles.lyzr: The platform, the templates to start from, and enablement for your team

revenue.implementation: The audit and its findings, then design, build, integration and deployment on the first {unit}
revenue.recurring: Running and supporting each {unit} once it is live, with changes as the process moves
revenue.expansion: The second {unit} as a shorter build, and the audit itself as the repeatable way in to the next client

patterns.when: The constraint is the environment rather than the workflow: regulated, sovereign, on-premise, or an architecture that has to be signed off before anything is built.

first_offer.name: {work} readiness review
first_offer.ends_with: what can run where, what the controls have to be, and a deployment plan their risk function can sign

delivery.shape: 10 to 12 week deployment on one {unit}, then infrastructure and support
delivery.team_needed: 1 solution architect + 1 infrastructure engineer + a compliance reviewer

patterns.expansion: A support and change contract on the environment, then the next workload into it
discovery: Where the data is allowed to live, and who decides that
What their risk or audit function has already asked about AI
Which environments are in scope, and who runs them
What has to be true before a decision can run without a person

roles.partner: The environment, the client's controls, the deployment and the ongoing support
roles.lyzr: The deployable platform, the governance layer and the architecture review

revenue.implementation: Readiness review, architecture, deployment into their environment, integration and commissioning
revenue.recurring: Infrastructure management, monitoring, patching and user support on the deployed environment
revenue.expansion: The next workload into the same environment, and a change contract as their estate grows

patterns.when: They have built much the same thing more than once for different clients. The question is whether it becomes a solution they sell into an industry rather than a project they re-quote every time.

first_offer.name: {work} solution blueprint
first_offer.ends_with: a packaged solution with a fixed scope, a working demo and a price, ready to take to the next three clients

delivery.shape: 8 week build of the packaged version, then a deployment fee per client

patterns.expansion: Every new client deploys the same package, so the build is paid for once and each further {unit} is margin
discovery: How many clients have asked for this {work} in the last year
What changed between the last two times you built it
Which part of it is the same for every client, and which is not
Who would buy it if it already existed and had a price

roles.partner: The repeatable solution, the industry knowledge, the sales motion and the deployments
roles.lyzr: The platform it is packaged on, the templates, and joint go-to-market on the first clients

revenue.implementation: The blueprint, then building the packaged version once: design, configuration, the integration points and the deployment method
revenue.recurring: Running the package for each client who takes it, with support and release management
revenue.expansion: Every new client deploys the same package, so each further {unit} is delivery rather than another build

patterns.when: The client already has AI running that nobody owns. The money is in the control layer over it, not in building more.

first_offer.name: Agent estate assessment
first_offer.ends_with: an inventory of every agent and copilot running, what each one can reach, and a registry pilot

delivery.shape: 4 week discovery and registry, then an annual platform and advisory fee

patterns.expansion: An annual platform fee plus a quarterly review covering new agents as they are added
discovery: How many teams have deployed something, and on how many platforms
Whether anyone owns AI risk formally, and who they report to
What the audit or regulator has already asked for
Which environments and data the running agents can reach

roles.partner: The governance engagement, the risk relationship and the consultants who run it
roles.lyzr: OpenController for the registry and the controls, and the policy layer

revenue.implementation: Discovery across their agent estate, the registry, policy and control setup, and the platform rollout
revenue.recurring: The platform itself, quarterly reviews, policy updates, and advisory as new agents are added
revenue.expansion: New agents and new teams brought under the same registry, and the same review extended to the next estate

patterns.when: Something is already live and fragile. The offer is to own it: monitoring, incidents, versions and a service level.

first_offer.name: {work} operations review
first_offer.ends_with: what is running, what is unmonitored, what has already broken, and a takeover plan

delivery.shape: Onboarding sprint to take it over, then a monthly fee per workload

patterns.expansion: The monthly fee grows with each new workload that goes live
discovery: What is running in production today, and who built it
Who gets called when it fails, and what their hours are
What has already gone wrong, and how they found out
What a service level would have to cover for them to sign

roles.partner: The support structure, the on-call rota and the client relationship
roles.lyzr: The platform, the observability and escalation into our engineering

revenue.implementation: The operations review, the onboarding sprint, the runbooks, and taking the workloads over cleanly
revenue.recurring: Running each workload, incident handling, tuning, reporting and user support
revenue.expansion: Each new workload that goes live joins the same contract

patterns.when: The client wants one capability in front of a whole workforce rather than one use case built well. The work is standing it up, agreeing what good looks like, and getting people to use it.

first_offer.name: {work} pilot department
first_offer.ends_with: one department live with usage measured and an adoption plan for the rest

delivery.shape: 6 to 8 week rollout across the first wave, then a per seat fee to run and support it
delivery.team_needed: 1 delivery lead + 1 engineer + 1 adoption or change person

patterns.expansion: Each further {unit} joins the same deployment, so the cost is in adoption rather than in another build
discovery: How many people would use this, and in which {unit} first
What they use today for the same thing, approved or not
Who owns employee tooling and can make it standard
What has to be true before the policy team signs it off

roles.partner: The rollout, the adoption programme, the integration into how people already work
roles.lyzr: The product, the governance underneath it, and support through the first wave

revenue.implementation: The pilot on one {unit}, then rollout across the first wave: configuration, integration, training and launch
revenue.recurring: Running and supporting the deployment, the adoption work, and changes as teams ask for them
revenue.expansion: Each further {unit} joins the same deployment, so the work is adoption rather than another build

patterns.when: The client cannot send the work anywhere else. The engagement is installing and commissioning something inside their own environment and proving the first workload on it.

first_offer.name: {work} deployment readiness review
first_offer.ends_with: a sited design, the prerequisites confirmed, and a commissioning plan with dates

delivery.shape: 8 to 12 week install and commissioning, then an annual operate and support contract
delivery.team_needed: 1 infrastructure architect + 1 engineer, with the client's platform team

patterns.expansion: Capacity grows with each further {unit} placed on the same footprint, under the same contract
discovery: Where it would physically sit, and who owns that space
Which workload has to stay inside the estate, and why
What the network and identity boundaries look like
Who signs off a change inside that environment

roles.partner: The siting, the installation, the integration into their estate and the local support
roles.lyzr: The appliance, the models and governance on it, and the engineering behind the commissioning

revenue.implementation: Deployment readiness review, install, commissioning, integration and handover inside their own environment
revenue.recurring: The operate and support contract on the footprint: monitoring, upgrades, capacity and user support
revenue.expansion: Each further {unit} placed on the same footprint, under the same contract

patterns.when: The partner ships software of their own. The work is putting a capability inside that product, under their brand, and selling it to the customers they already have.

first_offer.name: {work} embedding assessment
first_offer.ends_with: the integration mapped against their architecture, and a first feature scoped against their roadmap

delivery.shape: 10 to 12 week integration into their product, then a licence that scales with their customers
delivery.team_needed: 1 product owner + 2 engineers from their own product team

patterns.expansion: Every customer of their product reaches the capability, so revenue follows their install base rather than their delivery hours
discovery: What their product does today and who pays for it
Which {unit} the capability would land in first
How their release cycle and their tenancy model work
What they would have to build themselves instead, and how long it would take

roles.partner: The product, the customers, the roadmap and the first line of support
roles.lyzr: The platform layer underneath, the tenancy and governance, and the engineering behind the integration

revenue.implementation: The embedding assessment, integration into their product, and the engineering to ship it to their customers
revenue.recurring: Keeping the embedded capability current as their product and the models change, plus support
revenue.expansion: Revenue follows their install base rather than your delivery hours, so every customer of their product reaches the capability
